blocks.text: What this usually means in UK cars

ordered.title: Limp mode is a safety feature - it's protecting your engine
ordered.description: Think of it as your car saying: "Something is wrong. I'm limiting your speed so you can get to a garage - but I won't let you drive normally until it's fixed."

blocks.text: In our 24,650 quote dataset, we identified six primary causes of limp mode:

items: Sensor failure (30% of cases) - MAF, boost pressure, throttle position sensors. Repair: £100-£300.
DPF blockage (20% of cases, diesel) - Diesel particulate filter blocked. Repair: £100-£3,500.
Turbo/actuator issues (18% of cases) - Turbo vane sticking, actuator failure. Repair: £450-£3,000+.
EGR valve failure (12% of cases) - EGR stuck open/closed. Repair: £300-£600.
Injector/fuel system (10% of cases) - Fuel pressure issues. Repair: £300-£900.
Electrical/ECU issues (10% of cases) - Wiring, ECU, or CAN bus problems. Repair: £100-£1,200+.

blocks.text: The critical distinction: If limp mode clears after restarting and doesn't return, it might be a temporary glitch. If it returns immediately or consistently, you need a diagnostic.

Don't fall for these common misconceptions

cards.text: “Turning the car off and on resets it - I'll just keep driving.” If the underlying fault persists, it will return. You're driving a time bomb.
cards.fullText: “Turning the car off and on resets it - I'll just keep driving.” If the underlying fault persists, it will return. You're driving a time bomb.

cards.text: “Limp mode means my engine is destroyed.” Rarely. Limp mode is a protection mechanism - it prevents damage. Most repairs are £100-£600.

cards.text: “I can drive in limp mode for weeks.” You can drive at reduced speed to a garage. Continued driving can damage the DPF, turbo, or catalytic converter.

cards.text: “It's probably the turbo - that's expensive.” Sometimes. But 30% of cases are simple sensor failures (£100-£300). Get diagnosed first.

ordered.title: ⚠️ CAN YOU DRIVE IN LIMP MODE?
ordered.description: Yes - but ONLY to a garage.

items: ✅ DO: Drive to a garage at reduced speed
✅ DO: Avoid motorways or fast roads
✅ DO: Get it diagnosed promptly
❌ DON'T: Continue normal driving
❌ DON'T: Drive for days or weeks
❌ DON'T: Ignore it and hope it goes away

blocks.text: The Resetting Myth: "Turning the car off and on may temporarily clear limp mode, but if the underlying fault persists, it will return." The ECU doesn't forget the fault - it will enter limp mode again as soon as the condition is detected.

cards.title: What happens if you ignore it
cards.text: The £5,000 Mistake: Ignoring limp mode "because it clears on restart" is a common and costly error. What could have been a £100 sensor replacement becomes a £1,000+ DPF or £3,000+ turbo.

cards.title: What to do next
cards.text: Step 1: Don't Panic - It's A Safety Feature - Limp mode is protecting your engine. It's not the end of the world - it's a warning. Step 2: Drive To A Garage (If Safe) - Drive at reduced speed. Avoid motorways. Get it diagnosed promptly. Step 3: Get Professional Diagnostic (£50-£150) - A technician will read fault codes (this is crucial), check live data (sensor readings), and perform further tests based on codes. Important: A reset without diagnosis is pointless. Always get the fault codes read BEFORE resetting. Step 4: Get A Repair Quote - Once the cause is identified, you'll know if it's simple (£100-£300 sensor), moderate (£300-£600 EGR), or expensive (£450-£3,500+ turbo/DPF).

ordered.title: Limp mode rarely requires engine replacement
ordered.description: “Limp mode rarely requires engine replacement - it's almost always a sensor, EGR, DPF, or turbo issue. The repair cost depends on what failed.”

rows: Consider cost vs value if DPF or turbo.

ordered.title: Common affected engines and root causes

items: VAG 2.0 TDI (EA189): DPF blockage is the most common limp mode trigger - especially in city-driven vehicles. A forced regen (£100-£200) often fixes it if caught early.
BMW N47/N57: Boost pressure sensor failure is common - this is a £150-£300 fix, not a turbo replacement.
Ford 1.6/2.0 TDCi: EGR valve failure triggers limp mode. EGR replacement is £300-£600.
Mercedes OM651: NOx sensor failure is increasingly common and triggers limp mode. Replacement: £300-£700.
Land Rover SDV6: EGR cooler and DPF issues are common triggers. Both are expensive repairs: £500-£2,000.
VAG EA888 petrol: Throttle body and MAF sensor failures are common in 2.0 TSI engines. These are £150-£400 fixes.

blocks.text: Always read the fault codes BEFORE resetting. The codes tell the story. A reset without reading codes means you're flying blind.
Cost Disclaimer: Pricing is for UK independent specialists (2025-2026). Main dealers may charge 30-50% more. Regional variations apply. Costs exclude VAT unless stated.

blocks.question: How much does limp mode diagnosis cost in the UK?
blocks.answer: Limp mode diagnosis costs £50-£150 at UK independent garages. This includes reading fault codes and basic inspection.

blocks.question: Can I drive in limp mode?
blocks.answer: Yes - to a garage. Do not continue normal driving. Speed is limited to 30-50 mph.

blocks.question: Why does limp mode clear when I restart?
blocks.answer: Some faults are temporary - the ECU enters limp mode when it detects a problem but may clear it if the condition doesn't persist. But if the fault returns, it's a real issue.

blocks.question: How much does DPF replacement cost in the UK?
blocks.answer: DPF replacement costs £1,000-£3,500 depending on the vehicle. A forced regen (£100-£200) often fixes early-stage DPF blockages.

blocks.question: Is limp mode dangerous?
blocks.answer: Limp mode itself is a safety feature. But the cause - if ignored - can lead to engine failure. Get it diagnosed promptly.

blocks.question: How long can I drive in limp mode?
blocks.answer: Only as long as it takes to reach a garage. Continued driving risks damaging the DPF, turbo, or catalytic converter.

blocks.question: Can a sensor failure cause limp mode?
blocks.answer: Yes - this is the most common cause (30% of cases). A failing MAF, boost pressure, or throttle position sensor will trigger limp mode.
